metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Point of Rocks, WY
metaDescription: Own minerals near Point of Rocks, an old rail stop along the checkerboard in Sweetwater County? We confirm section-by-section ownership before pricing.
heroLead: Point of Rocks is an old railroad stop along the original Union Pacific line, and the checkerboard pattern that grant created runs right through the ground around it.
intro: This stretch of Sweetwater County sits squarely in the historic Union Pacific land grant, where odd-numbered sections went to the railroad and were later sold off privately, while even sections stayed federal, administered today by the BLM. That pattern decides more about a Point of Rocks mineral interest than almost anything else — which section your tract falls in changes who you deal with and what records exist.

The community itself grew up as a rail stop, and a lot of the private mineral title in the area traces directly back to those original railroad land sales rather than a homestead patent, which is a different chain of title than most of Wyoming.

sections.heading: Reading the checkerboard
paragraphs: Before we make an offer near Point of Rocks, we confirm whether your legal description falls in a historic railroad-grant section or a federal one. Private minerals in the odd sections are what we buy; federal sections belong to the government and are administered through BLM leasing, not private sale.

sections.heading: Gas production in the area
paragraphs: The broader area has seen gas development tied to the Green River Basin's Fort Union and related formations. We check current Wyoming Oil and Gas Conservation Commission filings for your specific tract to see if it sits inside an active unit.

sections.heading: Getting started
paragraphs: Send your legal description along with any division order or old lease you have, and we will confirm the section pattern and current activity before pricing.

faqs.question: How do I know if my section is railroad-grant private land or federal BLM land?
faqs.answer: We check your legal description against the historic checkerboard pattern and current BLM records to confirm.

faqs.question: If my section turns out to be federal, do I own anything?
faqs.answer: If it's federal land, the government owns the minerals, not you. But a lot of Point of Rocks-area sections are private, so it depends on your specific tract.

faqs.question: Is there active gas production near Point of Rocks?
faqs.answer: It varies by unit. We check current filings for your tract before making an offer.

faqs.question: How is a railroad-grant title chain different from a homestead one?
faqs.answer: Railroad-grant minerals trace back to the original Union Pacific patent and its later sales, rather than a settler's homestead claim, so the deed history runs through different records than most Wyoming ranch land.
